edges.sentence: On 2026-10-01, BBC reported “Last Friday, the commission decided that the march could go ahead with restrictions in place.”; on 2026-10-02, The Guardian reported “Last Friday’s Parades Commission decision to grant the Orange Order the right to hold a procession down the nationalist Garvaghy Road plunged Northern Ireland into one of its most perilous periods since the 1998 peace deal.”.

On 2026-10-01, BBC reported “Last Friday, the commission decided that the march could go ahead with restrictions in place.”; on 2026-10-02, The Guardian reported “The dispute began last week after the march along the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road was given the go-ahead by the Parades Commission for the first time since 1998, a decision denounced by Sinn Féin as “madness” and by the taoiseach as “incomprehensible and wrong”.”.

On 2026-10-01, BBC reported “Last Friday, the commission decided that the march could go ahead with restrictions in place.”; on the same day, BBC reported “However, that decision was challenged in several Belfast courts on Saturday, before finally being given the go-ahead just hours before it was due to take place.”.

On 2026-10-02, The Guardian reported “Last Friday’s Parades Commission decision to grant the Orange Order the right to hold a procession down the nationalist Garvaghy Road plunged Northern Ireland into one of its most perilous periods since the 1998 peace deal.”; on 2026-10-01, BBC reported “However, that decision was challenged in several Belfast courts on Saturday, before finally being given the go-ahead just hours before it was due to take place.”.

On 2026-10-02, The Guardian reported “Last Friday’s Parades Commission decision to grant the Orange Order the right to hold a procession down the nationalist Garvaghy Road plunged Northern Ireland into one of its most perilous periods since the 1998 peace deal.”; on the same day, The Guardian reported “The dispute began last week after the march along the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road was given the go-ahead by the Parades Commission for the first time since 1998, a decision denounced by Sinn Féin as “madness” and by the taoiseach as “incomprehensible and wrong”.”.

On 2026-10-02, The Guardian reported “The dispute began last week after the march along the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road was given the go-ahead by the Parades Commission for the first time since 1998, a decision denounced by Sinn Féin as “madness” and by the taoiseach as “incomprehensible and wrong”.”; on 2026-10-01, BBC reported “However, that decision was challenged in several Belfast courts on Saturday, before finally being given the go-ahead just hours before it was due to take place.”.
